Senses.PreferredTarget: a settled footing for one's life
AlternateTargets: a place to stand and live
Senses.Note: The records repeatedly ask where such a footing is found and overturn proposed places; the phrase does not itself certify that any offered position is secure.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂。僧問。橫穿碧落倒卓須彌。未審是什麼人分上事。師云。入地獄人分上事。進云。却是他安身立命處。師云。瓦解氷消。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1997.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo. An unnamed monk proposes that this is another person's settled footing; Yuanwu Keqin answers that tile and ice dissolve.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 進云 introduces the monk's exact headword-bearing proposal, and 師云 immediately after it transfers the next turn to Yuanwu Keqin.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若揀得出。非唯親見香嚴。亦使虎頭上座無安身立命處。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1998A.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue. Dahui Zonggao says that sorting out the two dangers would leave the named head monk with no settled footing.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云。室生虛白。眼照清光。猶未是衲僧安身立命處。且道。畢竟作麼生。良久云。三更月落夜巢寒。瓊林不宿千年鶴。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T48/T48n2001.xml). Extensive Record of Chan Master Hongzhi. Hongzhi Zhengjue says that a chamber filled with clarity is still not a patch-robed monk's settled footing, then asks what finally is.

Occurrences.Kwic: 苟或箇箇如此。山僧且打退鼓。諸人向什麼處。安身立命岌崿。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T48/T48n2003.xml). Blue Cliff Record by Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo. Yuanwu Keqin asks the assembly where they will establish a settled footing after saying he would beat the retreat drum.

Occurrences.Kwic: 且問儞等諸人向甚麼處安身立命？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X79/X79n1557.xml). Essential Compendium of the United Lamp. Shishuang Chuyuan asks the assembly where they settle themselves and establish their lives.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問生死到來如何迴避。師曰。定花板上。曰莫便是他安身立命處也無。師曰。符到奉行。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T51/T51n2077.xml). Continued Record of the Transmission of the Lamp. An unnamed monk asks whether the master's first answer is precisely the settled footing in question; the master answers again.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The sequence 問…師曰…曰…師曰 marks the headword-bearing middle 曰 as the unnamed monk's follow-up question.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。學人不據地時如何。師曰。汝向甚麼處安身立命。曰。却據地時如何。師曰。拖出死屍著。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X80/X80n1565.xml). Five Lamps Compendium. Changsha Jingcen asks where the monk will establish a settled footing when he does not rely on the ground.

Senses.Explanation: A settled footing for one's life is what the Chan record repeatedly demands when it asks where someone can stand and live after an offered ground or position has been removed. Changsha Jingcen asks a monk who claims not to rely on the ground where he will establish such a footing. Yuanwu Keqin records a monk proposing one, then answers that it dissolves like tile and ice; elsewhere Yuanwu asks an assembly the same where-question. Hongzhi Zhengjue says that even a chamber filled with clarity is not yet a patch-robed monk's settled footing. Shishuang Chuyuan puts the question directly to everyone present, so the phrase works as a public test rather than a promise that any stated place is secure.
